answer: To join, a new identity passes a layered karst audit: documents, then a work trail, then a live task re-run by an independent auditor — the echo test. It also needs three sponsors, each staking 20 POA; any mismatch burns all three stakes plus the identity's own 30 POA bond. Sponsorship fees rise quadratically: the k-th identity one sponsor backs in an epoch costs 5k² POA, so 10 names cost 1,925 POA in fees and 300 POA in bonds against 250 POA of rewards. The old fable that fresh names equal real people dies here: honest sponsors back few real names, while farms pay the square of their greed.
